selected.title: Her Boss Told Me We Were Moving to Chicago
selected.hook: My girlfriend's new boss congratulated me on our move to Chicago.
selected.voiceover:
My girlfriend's new boss congratulated me on our move to Chicago. The problem was, I had no idea we were moving.

I met him at her company's summer party. He shook my hand and said, "You must be excited for January."

I thought he meant the new year.

Then he said they'd already approved her transfer.

She pulled me aside immediately.

For six months, we'd been talking about renewing our lease and saving for a bigger place. Apparently, during those conversations, she'd applied for a promotion three states away.

And she got it.

She said she hadn't told me because nothing was guaranteed. Fair enough—until I learned she'd accepted the offer two weeks earlier.

Her start date was set. HR had relocation paperwork. She'd even toured apartments during a "girls' weekend" I helped her pack for.

When I asked where I fit into this plan, she said she assumed I'd come because my job was remote.

That sentence changed everything.

She hadn't been deciding whether to move. She'd been deciding for both of us, then waiting to present it like a shared opportunity.

I left the party alone.

Now she's saying I'm focusing on the secrecy instead of the promotion she's worked years for.

I'm proud of her. I just don't know if I can build a future with someone who plans our future without me.

Would you move with her, or would the secret decision end it?
selected.youtube_description:
At his girlfriend's company party, her boss casually congratulated him on their upcoming move to Chicago. There was just one problem: nobody had told him they were moving. What follows turns a career promotion into a much bigger relationship question about secrecy, shared decisions, and whether one partner can plan a future for two people.
